items.name: Convert Image
items.description: A utility step that re-encodes an image to a target format (JPEG, PNG, WebP, or GIF) and optionally applies ordered transforms such as aspect-ratio-preserving resize and rectangular region blur before encoding. Metadata can be stripped on output; results are deterministic and cached.

items.name: Text to Image (Deprecated)
items.description: Legacy generic text-to-image step that runs a checkpoint model — Stable Diffusion, Flux, Qwen, and others — with optional additional networks such as LoRAs. Deprecated and being phased out: new integrations should call the dedicated per-model image services (for example the Flux, Qwen-Image, or SDXL endpoints) rather than this generic step.

items.name: Transcode
items.description: Re-encodes a source video into a target container format at a specified width, producing a normalized output clip. Commonly used to standardize or downscale footage before other processing steps.

items.name: WD Tagging
items.description: Runs Waifu Diffusion (WD) tagging on an image to produce a list of descriptive tags identifying characteristics, objects, and themes, with an optional confidence threshold. Output is text tags.

items.name: Media Rating
items.description: Classifies media for NSFW level and content safety, returning a rating and safety labels for the input image. Used as a content-moderation classifier.

items.name: Video Frame Extraction
items.description: Extracts frames from a video at a configurable frame rate and removes near-duplicates using perceptual hashing, returning a set of unique still images. An optional cap limits the number of frames extracted.

items.name: Media Hash
items.description: Computes perceptual hashes of an image or video for deduplication and similarity matching. The set of hash types to generate is configurable, and the result is returned as hash strings.

items.name: Comfy
items.description: Executes an orchestrator-composed ComfyUI workflow graph on a GPU worker and returns the generated media blobs. Required resources such as checkpoints and LoRAs are declared up front, and the output slots are verified on success.

items.name: Anima · Create Image
items.description: Anima is an open-weights 2-billion-parameter anime and illustration model from CircleStone Labs (with Comfy Org), trained on millions of anime images plus artistic non-anime data. It is served on Civitai for text-to-image generation and supports LoRAs for style and character control.
items.strengths: Tuned for anime and illustration across a wide range of characters and styles; supports stacking LoRAs for style and character injection; works well at common aspect ratios near one megapixel.
items.weaknesses: Not suited to photorealism — output stays illustrative; a lower guidance scale than SD-family models is needed for on-style results.

items.name: Media Captioning
items.description: Generates a descriptive natural-language caption for a single image using the JoyCaption model, with optional custom instructions. Output is text.

items.name: Krea 2 Turbo
items.description: Krea 2 is a text-to-image model from Krea, built from scratch as a 12-billion-parameter diffusion transformer with an emphasis on aesthetics and style control. It ships as a Raw checkpoint intended for fine-tuning and LoRA training and a distilled Turbo checkpoint for fast inference. (8-step distilled checkpoint for fast inference)
items.strengths: Aesthetics-oriented output with style-reference and moodboard controls; the Turbo variant generates images in roughly two seconds; the Raw variant supports fine-tuning and LoRA training.
items.weaknesses: The distilled Turbo checkpoint trades some fine detail and prompt precision for its fast, few-step inference.

items.name: Repeat
items.description: A control-flow utility that fans a template step out over an array, generating one child step per item. It dispatches no jobs itself; cost and output come from the generated child steps.

items.name: Image Upload
items.description: A utility step that ingests a caller-supplied image (URL, data URL, or Base64) into workflow blob storage so it can be referenced by later steps, returning the stored blob reference.

items.name: Z-Image Turbo
items.description: Z-Image is Tongyi-MAI's (Alibaba) open-weights 6-billion-parameter single-stream diffusion transformer. The Turbo checkpoint is an 8-step distilled variant for fast, low-cost text-to-image generation that fits within 16GB of VRAM.
items.strengths: Photorealistic output and accurate bilingual English/Chinese text rendering; strong prompt adherence; the Turbo variant generates in as few as 8 steps within 16GB of VRAM, and the Base model is fine-tunable and supports LoRAs.
items.weaknesses: Produces less diverse output than the Base model and effectively ignores negative prompts at its near-zero guidance; tuned for English and Chinese, so other languages degrade.

items.name: Prompt Moderation
items.description: Evaluates generation prompts (positive and negative) against XGuard content-moderation policies, scoring configurable safety labels with logprob-based classification and returning per-label results.

items.name: Model Parse Metadata
items.description: Extracts the embedded JSON metadata header from a safetensors model file and returns it as text.

items.name: Model Hash
items.description: Computes content hashes of a model file, including SHA256, AutoV1/AutoV2/AutoV3, Blake3, and CRC32, and returns them as text.

items.name: Model Pickle Scan
items.description: Scans a model file with picklescan to detect dangerous or unexpected pickle imports that could execute code when the file is loaded, and returns the scan result.

items.name: Model Clam Scan
items.description: Scans a model file with ClamAV for known malware signatures and returns the scan result.

items.name: Stable Diffusion XL · Create Image
items.description: Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) is an open-weights latent diffusion text-to-image model from Stability AI with a 1024x1024 native resolution and dual text encoders. It succeeds the Stable Diffusion 1.x family and supports LoRAs, textual-inversion embeddings, and image-to-image variants.
items.strengths: Large community catalog of fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRAs; accepts both tag-style and natural-language prompts; produces 1-megapixel images and handles a range of near-square aspect ratios.
items.weaknesses: Weak at rendering legible text; aspect ratios far from square can produce duplicated or mirrored subjects; no prompt-driven editing operation; newer families offer stronger prompt adherence.

items.name: LTX-2.3 · First-Last Frame to Video
items.description: LTX (LTX Video) is Lightricks' open-weights video generation family, running on Civitai's ComfyUI workers. LTX-2 adds synchronized audio and higher-resolution output; LTX-2.3 adds video-to-video style transfer and audio-driven talking-head generation. Operations span text-, image-, first/last-frame-, and video-to-video.
items.strengths: Broad operation set (text-to-video, image-to-video, first/last-frame interpolation, extend, edit, video-to-video, audio-to-video); community LoRA support; synchronized audio in LTX-2.3; generally the lowest-cost video path on the platform.
items.weaknesses: Accepts only fixed clip durations (3 or 20 seconds); distilled model variants trade fidelity for speed; as an open model it can trail leading commercial systems on some quality benchmarks.

items.name: Qwen-Image Qwen2 · Edit Image
items.description: Qwen-Image is Alibaba's 20-billion-parameter open-weights image model for text-to-image generation and editing. It is noted for rendering text, including Chinese, inside images. Civitai serves it on self-hosted sdcpp workers and through a hosted path with an additional Pro tier. (hosted Qwen-Image path, including a commercial Pro tier.)
items.strengths: Complex text rendering, including Chinese, natural-language prompt adherence, and LoRA support on the self-hosted path.
items.weaknesses: Trained around 1-megapixel output, so very high resolutions require upscaling.

items.name: Prompt Enhancement
items.description: Rewrites a user-written prompt for a specific generation ecosystem (for example sd1, sdxl, flux1, or ltx2) using a language model, returning detected issues, recommendations, and an enhanced prompt, plus an enhanced negative prompt when a negative prompt is supplied.

items.name: FLUX.2 Klein 9B · Edit Image
items.description: FLUX.2 [klein] is Black Forest Labs' distilled, open-weights branch of FLUX.2, released January 2026 for fast generation on consumer GPUs. It ships in 4B (Apache 2.0) and 9B sizes, supports LoRAs, and handles text-to-image, editing, and image-to-image. On Civitai it is the default FLUX.2 variant. (open weights, non-commercial license; higher fidelity at higher cost)
items.strengths: Fast, low-cost generation on consumer hardware; open weights with LoRA and edit-training support; covers create, edit and variant operations; strong quality for high-volume workloads.
items.weaknesses: As a distilled model it trades peak fidelity against the full FLUX.2 [dev] and [pro] tiers; the base checkpoints are un-tuned, intended for fine-tuning rather than direct generation.

(Seedream 4.5; refined v4 with stronger typography and subject consistency. Platform default.)
items.strengths: Native high-resolution output up to 4096 pixels per side, multilingual text rendering, and multi-image reference editing.
items.weaknesses: Output can appear over-saturated at high guidance values.

items.weaknesses: Feature and operation support varies significantly across the different versions.

items.weaknesses: Higher-resolution output is slower to generate, and long or complex in-image text can still show minor errors.

items.name: LoRA Training · SDXL
items.description: Civitai's LoRA and fine-tune training service. Each entry trains a LoRA (or fine-tune) on a user-supplied dataset for one base-model ecosystem, using the AI Toolkit, Kohya, or Musubi open-source trainers. Output is a downloadable model (typically.safetensors) usable in the matching generation workflows.
items.strengths: Covers a broad range of image, video, and audio base-model ecosystems through a shared request schema; delivers multiple saved checkpoints per run; supports resuming from a previously trained LoRA and a preview (whatif) cost check before submitting.

items.strengths: Strong prompt adherence and motion dynamics; Standard and Professional quality modes; camera-control axes for directed motion; V3 adds synchronized audio and time-sequenced multi-prompt generation.

(Reve Image 1.0, codenamed Halfmoon; first release from Reve AI)

items.weaknesses: Exposes fewer resolution and aspect-ratio controls than larger commercial image families.

items.name: FLUX.2 Flex · Edit Image
items.description: FLUX.2 is Black Forest Labs' second-generation text-to-image and image-editing family, released November 2025. It adds multi-reference conditioning of up to 10 images, higher fidelity, and improved text rendering. Tiers span the open-weights [dev], the tunable [flex], and the commercial [pro] and [max] API models. (tunable mid-tier; faster than dev with fewer knobs)

items.name: ERNIE-Image Turbo
items.description: ERNIE-Image is Baidu's open-weights text-to-image model, built on an 8-billion-parameter single-stream Diffusion Transformer with a prompt-enhancer. It targets text-in-image tasks such as posters, comics, and storyboards, and ships standard and distilled turbo variants. Only text-to-image generation is supported. (ERNIE-Image-Turbo; distilled variant generating in roughly 8 steps.)
items.strengths: Accurate dense text rendering inside images, complex multi-object instruction following, and structured layouts such as posters and storyboards. Runs on consumer GPUs and offers a distilled turbo variant.
items.weaknesses: Supports only text-to-image generation, with no editing, variation, or inpainting. Trained around 1-megapixel output; the turbo variant does not respond to classifier-free guidance.

items.weaknesses: As a distilled model it trades peak fidelity against the full FLUX.2 [dev] and [pro] tiers; the base checkpoints are un-tuned, intended for fine-tuning rather than direct generation.

items.name: Ideogram 4.0
items.description: Ideogram 4.0 is a text-to-image model from Ideogram, run on Civitai-hosted ComfyUI workers. It is a 9.3-billion-parameter diffusion transformer trained from scratch, noted for text rendering and typography, with native 2K resolution, JSON-based layout control, and alpha-channel output.
items.strengths: Legible text rendering and typography; native 2K resolution; JSON layout control for precise composition; native alpha-channel output for clean cutouts without a separate background-removal pass.
items.weaknesses: Ranks below leading closed models from OpenAI and Google on general text-to-image benchmarks; oriented toward design and typography rather than photorealism.

items.name: Lens
items.description: Lens is an open-weights 3.8-billion-parameter text-to-image model using a dual-stream MMDiT with GPT-OSS-20B text features and the FLUX.2 semantic VAE. The standard variant runs the full sampling schedule (around 20 steps) for maximum quality.
items.strengths: Efficient high-resolution text-to-image from a compact 3.8B model; competitive quality for its size; the Turbo variant generates in about four steps.

items.name: OmniSVG
items.description: OmniSVG is a research model for scalable vector graphics (SVG) generation built on pre-trained vision-language models. It autoregressively generates SVG code across a wide range of complexity, from simple icons to detailed illustrations, and supports text-to-SVG, image-to-SVG, and character-reference generation.
items.strengths: Generates structured, editable SVG code rather than raster images; spans a wide complexity range from icons to detailed illustrations; supports text, image, and character-reference inputs.
items.weaknesses: A research model rather than a production service; autoregressive token-by-token SVG generation is sequential and can be slow for complex outputs; fidelity varies with input.

items.name: Stable Diffusion 1.5 · Create Image
items.description: Stable Diffusion 1.x is an open-weights latent diffusion text-to-image model family with a 512x512 native resolution. Version 1.5, released by RunwayML, became the community's dominant base model, with a large catalog of fine-tuned checkpoints, LoRAs, and textual-inversion embeddings.
items.strengths: Very large, mature catalog of fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRAs; low compute cost and fast generation at 512x512; supports textual-inversion embeddings and clip-skip control.
items.weaknesses: Low 512x512 native resolution and dated image quality relative to SDXL and later models; weak text rendering and prompt adherence; higher resolutions require upscaling and can introduce composition artifacts.

items.weaknesses: A research model rather than a production service; sequential code generation can be slow, and very complex images may not vectorize cleanly.

It takes a text instruction plus one or more reference images to edit while preserving characters and style, and can also generate from text alone. Offered in [pro] and [max] commercial tiers and an open-weights [dev] tier. (open-weights, ~12B parameters; cheapest Kontext option)

items.description: Detects the likely presence of minors in media using SigLIP2-based age and face-recognition models, returning whether minors are detected along with per-detection details. Can fail the step when minors are detected above configured thresholds.

items.name: Batch OCR Safety Classification
items.description: Extracts text from a batch of images via OCR and classifies it for safety, returning per-image safety results. Preview feature.

items.name: Qwen Image Bench
items.description: Scores generated images against the prompts that produced them using the Qwen-Image-Bench judge model, across dimensions such as Quality, Aesthetics, Alignment, Real-world Fidelity, and Creative Generation. Each prompt/image pair is evaluated independently; output is text scores.

items.name: Compose Media
items.description: Composites multiple audio and video elements onto a single timeline and canvas, mixing audio and layering video by z-order. Produces a video when any element is video, otherwise an audio mixdown. Supports per-element placement, transforms, and background removal.

items.name: Echo
items.description: A testing utility that returns the input message unchanged. Used to exercise the workflow pipeline without performing real work.

items.name: Comfy Video
items.description: Generates video from a text prompt, with an optional source image, by running a ComfyUI pipeline on a GPU worker. Checkpoint and LoRA resources, sampler, resolution, frame rate, and duration are configurable. Currently a preview engine.

items.name: Haiper
items.description: Haiper is a commercial, API-only video generation model from Haiper AI, a London-based startup founded by former DeepMind researchers. Haiper 2.0, released October 2024, improved realism and temporal coherence and reduced generation time. Supports text-to-video and image-to-video.
items.strengths: Improved realism and temporal coherence in Haiper 2.0; faster generation than the prior version; supports both text-to-video and image-to-video.
items.weaknesses: An older model that produces only short clips and trails current video systems on realism and detail.

items.name: HappyHorse v1.0 · Reference to Video
items.description: HappyHorse is Alibaba's (Taotian Group) video model, served on Civitai as a hosted service. A unified 15-billion-parameter transformer generates video and synchronized native audio in a single pass, with multilingual lip-sync. Operations include text-to-video, image-to-video, subject reference with up to nine characters, and video editing.
items.strengths: Generates video with synchronized native audio in a single pass; multilingual lip-sync; subject consistency from up to nine character references; 1080p output; topped Artificial Analysis text-to-video and image-to-video preference rankings at launch.

items.description: LTX (LTX Video) is Lightricks' open-weights video generation family, running on Civitai's ComfyUI workers. LTX-2 adds synchronized audio and higher-resolution output; LTX-2.3 adds video-to-video style transfer and audio-driven talking-head generation. Operations span text-, image-, first/last-frame-, and video-to-video.

items.weaknesses: Accepts only fixed clip durations (3 or 20 seconds); distilled model variants trade fidelity for speed; as an open model it can trail leading commercial systems on some quality benchmarks.
